newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy deficit/GDP ratio must be 3pct in 97 - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy deficit/GDP ratio must be 3pct in 97 - Ciampi.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi was quoted as saying on Thursday that Italy's deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) ratio had to reach three percent in 1997, as required by the Maastricht Treaty for countries wishing to join a European single currency.
Ciampi, in an interview with Panorama magazine released ahead of publication, said the initial 1997 budget would reduce the deficit/GDP ratio to 4.5 percent.
"With the second phase we must reach the three percent (target) as called for by Maastricht," Ciampi answered in response to a question on what were the government's 1997 goals.
Ciampi said he hoped much of the additional reduction in the ratio would be brought about by a fall in interest rates.
"Certainly we can't reduce debt accumulated in previous years, but we can reduce interest rates through what we call a 'credibility operation'," Ciampi said.
"Every percentage point reduction in interest rates saves us 20 trillion lire over three and a half years -- more than five trillion in the first year," he added.

But Ciampi said he thought there might be a reevaluation of the Maastricht criteria which will be used to decide which countries can sign up to the planned launch of the single European currency in 1999.

"Let us not forget that the parameters are not barricades but reference points...In the Maastricht Treaty there is a clear indication that (economic) tendencies have to be taken into consideration," he told Panorama. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
